Name: Planning - Experimental Design
Learning Outcomes: Learners should be able to demonstrate and apply their knowledge and understanding of: experimental design
Description: including to solve problems set in a practical context.

Name: Planning - Control Variables
Learning Outcomes: Learners should be able to demonstrate and apply their knowledge and understanding of: identification of variables that must be controlled where appropriate.

Name: Planning - Method Evaluation
Learning Outcomes: Learners should be able to demonstrate and apply their knowledge and understanding of: evaluation that an experimental method is appropriate to meet the expected outcomes.

Name: Implementing - Apparatus and Techniques
Learning Outcomes: Learners should be able to demonstrate and apply their knowledge and understanding of: how to use a wide range of practical apparatus and techniques correctly.

Name: Implementing - Measurement Units
Learning Outcomes: Learners should be able to demonstrate and apply their knowledge and understanding of: appropriate units for measurements.

Name: Implementing - Data Presentation
Learning Outcomes: Learners should be able to demonstrate and apply their knowledge and understanding of: presenting observations and data in an appropriate format.

Name: Analysis - Result Processing
Learning Outcomes: Learners should be able to demonstrate and apply their knowledge and understanding of: processing analysing and interpreting qualitative and quantitative experimental results.

Name: Analysis - Mathematical Skills
Learning Outcomes: Learners should be able to demonstrate and apply their knowledge and understanding of: use of appropriate mathematical skills for analysis of quantitative data.

Name: Analysis - Significant Figures
Learning Outcomes: Learners should be able to demonstrate and apply their knowledge and understanding of: appropriate use of significant figures.

Name: Analysis - Graph Plotting (Axes)
Learning Outcomes: Learners should be able to demonstrate and apply their knowledge and understanding of: plotting and interpreting suitable graphs from experimental results including selection and labelling of axes with appropriate scales quantities and units.

Name: Analysis - Graph Plotting (Gradients)
Learning Outcomes: Learners should be able to demonstrate and apply their knowledge and understanding of: plotting and interpreting suitable graphs from experimental results including measurement of gradients and intercepts.

Name: Evaluation - Drawing Conclusions
Learning Outcomes: Learners should be able to demonstrate and apply their knowledge and understanding of: how to evaluate results and draw conclusions.

Name: Evaluation - Anomaly Identification
Learning Outcomes: Learners should be able to demonstrate and apply their knowledge and understanding of: the identification of anomalies in experimental measurements.

Name: Evaluation - Procedure Limitations
Learning Outcomes: Learners should be able to demonstrate and apply their knowledge and understanding of: the limitations in experimental procedures.

Name: Evaluation - Precision and Accuracy
Learning Outcomes: Learners should be able to demonstrate and apply their knowledge and understanding of: precision and accuracy of measurements and data including margins of error percentage errors and uncertainties in apparatus.

Name: Evaluation - Refining Design
Learning Outcomes: Learners should be able to demonstrate and apply their knowledge and understanding of: the refining of experimental design by suggestion of improvements to the procedures and apparatus.

Name: Practical Skills - Investigative Approaches
Learning Outcomes: Practical work carried out throughout the course will enable learners to develop the following skills: apply investigative approaches and methods to practical work including how to solve problems in a practical context.

Name: Practical Skills - Equipment Safety
Learning Outcomes: Practical work carried out throughout the course will enable learners to develop the following skills: safely and correctly use a range of practical equipment and materials including identification of potential hazards and risk minimisation.

Name: Practical Skills - Written Instructions
Learning Outcomes: Practical work carried out throughout the course will enable learners to develop the following skills: follow written instructions.

Name: Practical Skills - Observations and Measurements
Learning Outcomes: Practical work carried out throughout the course will enable learners to develop the following skills: make and record observations/measurements.

Name: Practical Skills - Record Keeping
Learning Outcomes: Practical work carried out throughout the course will enable learners to develop the following skills: keep appropriate records of experimental activities.

Name: Practical Skills - Data Presentation
Learning Outcomes: Practical work carried out throughout the course will enable learners to develop the following skills: present information and data in a scientific way.

Name: Practical Skills - Software and Tools
Learning Outcomes: Practical work carried out throughout the course will enable learners to develop the following skills: use appropriate software and tools to process data carry out research and report findings.

Name: Practical Skills - Research Skills
Learning Outcomes: Practical work carried out throughout the course will enable learners to develop the following skills: use online and offline research skills including websites textbooks and other printed scientific sources of information.

Name: Practical Skills - Citing Sources
Learning Outcomes: Practical work carried out throughout the course will enable learners to develop the following skills: correctly cite sources of information using appropriate methods.

Name: Practical Skills - Instrument Selection
Learning Outcomes: Practical work carried out throughout the course will enable learners to develop the following skills: use a wide range of experimental and practical instruments equipment and techniques appropriate to the knowledge and understanding.

Name: Apparatus & Techniques - Quantitative Measurements
Learning Outcomes: Learners should be able to demonstrate skills through: use of appropriate apparatus to record a range of quantitative measurements (to include mass time volume temperature length and pH).

Name: Apparatus & Techniques - Instrumentation
Learning Outcomes: Learners should be able to demonstrate skills through: use of appropriate instrumentation to record quantitative measurements such as a colorimeter or potometer.

Name: Apparatus & Techniques - Glassware & Dilutions
Learning Outcomes: Learners should be able to demonstrate skills through: use of laboratory glassware apparatus for a variety of experimental techniques to include serial dilutions.

Name: Apparatus & Techniques - Microscope & Graticule
Learning Outcomes: Learners should be able to demonstrate skills through: use of a light microscope at high power and low power including use of a graticule.

Name: Apparatus & Techniques - Scientific Drawings
Learning Outcomes: Learners should be able to demonstrate skills through: production of scientific drawings from observations with annotations.

Name: Apparatus & Techniques - Qualitative Reagents
Learning Outcomes: Learners should be able to demonstrate skills through: use of qualitative reagents to identify biological molecules.

Name: Apparatus & Techniques - Chromatography & Electrophoresis
Learning Outcomes: Learners should be able to demonstrate skills through: separation of biological compounds using thin layer/paper chromatography or electrophoresis.

Name: Apparatus & Techniques - Organism Use (Responses)
Learning Outcomes: Learners should be able to demonstrate skills through: safe and ethical use of organisms to measure plant or animal responses.

Name: Apparatus & Techniques - Organism Use (Physiology)
Learning Outcomes: Learners should be able to demonstrate skills through: safe and ethical use of organisms to measure physiological functions.

Name: Apparatus & Techniques - Aseptic Techniques
Learning Outcomes: Learners should be able to demonstrate skills through: use of microbiological aseptic techniques including the use of agar plates and broth.

Name: Apparatus & Techniques - Dissection
Learning Outcomes: Learners should be able to demonstrate skills through: safe use of instruments for dissection of an animal or plant organ.

Name: Apparatus & Techniques - Fieldwork Sampling
Learning Outcomes: Learners should be able to demonstrate skills through: use of sampling techniques in fieldwork.

Name: Apparatus & Techniques - ICT & Data Loggers
Learning Outcomes: Learners should be able to demonstrate skills through: use of ICT such as computer modelling or a data logger to collect data or use of software to process data.

Name: Cell Structure - Microscopy Observation
Learning Outcomes: The use of microscopy to observe and investigate different types of cell and cell structure in a range of eukaryotic organisms
Description: To include an appreciation of the images produced by a range of microscopes; light microscope; transmission electron microscope and scanning electron microscope.

Name: Cell Structure - Slide Preparation
Learning Outcomes: The preparation and examination of microscope slides for use in light microscopy
Description: Including the use of an eye piece graticule and stage micrometer.

Name: Cell Structure - Staining
Learning Outcomes: The use of staining in light microscopy
Description: To include the use of differential staining to identify different cellular components and cell types.

Name: Cell Structure - Drawing and Diagrams
Learning Outcomes: The representation of cell structure as seen under the light microscope using drawings and annotated diagrams of whole cells or cells in sections of tissue
Description: As outlined in additional specification guidance.

Name: Cell Structure - Magnification Formula
Learning Outcomes: The use and manipulation of the magnification formula
Description: magnification = size of image / size of real object

Name: Cell Structure - Magnification vs Resolution
Learning Outcomes: The difference between magnification and resolution
Description: To include an appreciation of the differences in resolution and magnification that can be achieved by a light microscope; a transmission electron microscope and a scanning electron microscope.

Name: Cell Structure - Eukaryotic Ultrastructure
Learning Outcomes: The ultrastructure of eukaryotic cells and the functions of the different cellular components
Description: To include the following cellular components and an outline of their functions: nucleus; nucleolus; nuclear envelope; rough and smooth endoplasmic reticulum (ER); Golgi apparatus; ribosomes; mitochondria; lysosomes; chloroplasts; plasma membrane; centrioles; cell wall; flagella and cilia.

Name: Cell Structure - Photomicrographs
Learning Outcomes: Photomicrographs of cellular components in a range of eukaryotic cells
Description: To include interpretation of transmission and scanning electron microscope images.

Name: Cell Structure - Protein Secretion
Learning Outcomes: The interrelationship between the organelles involved in the production and secretion of proteins
Description: As outlined in additional specification guidance.

Name: Cell Structure - Cytoskeleton
Learning Outcomes: The importance of the cytoskeleton
Description: To include providing mechanical strength to cells; aiding transport within cells and enabling cell movement.

Name: Cell Structure - Prokaryotic vs Eukaryotic
Learning Outcomes: The similarities and differences in the structure and ultrastructure of prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells
Description: As outlined in additional specification guidance.

Name: Biological Molecules - Hydrogen Bonding and Water
Learning Outcomes: How hydrogen bonding occurs between water molecules and relate this and other properties of water to the roles of water for living organisms
Description: To include roles that relate to the properties of water; solvent; transport medium; coolant and as a habitat AND roles illustrated using examples of prokaryotes and eukaryotes.

Name: Biological Molecules - Monomers and Polymers
Learning Outcomes: The concept of monomers and polymers and the importance of condensation and hydrolysis reactions in a range of biological molecules
Description: Learners should be able to apply their knowledge and understanding in the context of prokaryotes and eukaryotes.

Name: Biological Molecules - Chemical Elements
Learning Outcomes: The chemical elements that make up biological molecules
Description: To include: C, H and O for carbohydrates; C, H and O for lipids; C, H, O, N and S for proteins; C, H, O, N and P for nucleic acids.

Name: Biological Molecules - Carbohydrate Ring Structures
Learning Outcomes: The ring structure and properties of glucose as an example of a hexose monosaccharide and the structure of ribose as an example of a pentose monosaccharide
Description: To include the structural difference between an alpha- and a beta-glucose molecule AND the difference between a hexose and a pentose monosaccharide.

Name: Biological Molecules - Glycosidic Bonds
Learning Outcomes: The synthesis and breakdown of a disaccharide and polysaccharide by the formation and breakage of glycosidic bonds
Description: To include the disaccharides sucrose; lactose and maltose.

Name: Biological Molecules - Polysaccharide Structures
Learning Outcomes: The structure of starch (amylose and amylopectin) glycogen and cellulose molecules
Description: As outlined in additional specification guidance.

Name: Biological Molecules - Carbohydrate Function
Learning Outcomes: How the structures and properties of glucose starch glycogen and cellulose molecules relate to their functions in living organisms
Description: As outlined in additional specification guidance.

Name: Biological Molecules - Lipid Structure
Learning Outcomes: The structure of a triglyceride and a phospholipid as examples of macromolecules
Description: To include the structure of saturated and unsaturated fatty acids.

Name: Biological Molecules - Ester Bonds
Learning Outcomes: The synthesis and breakdown of triglycerides by the formation and breakage of ester bonds between fatty acids and glycerol
Description: As outlined in additional specification guidance.

Name: Biological Molecules - Macromolecule Roles
Learning Outcomes: How the properties of triglyceride phospholipid and cholesterol molecules relate to their functions in living organisms
Description: To include hydrophobic and hydrophilic regions and energy content. Learners should be able to apply their knowledge and understanding in the context of prokaryotes and eukaryotes.

Name: Biological Molecules - Amino Acid Structure
Learning Outcomes: The general structure of an amino acid
Description: As outlined in additional specification guidance.

Name: Biological Molecules - Peptide Bonds
Learning Outcomes: The synthesis and breakdown of dipeptides and polypeptides by the formation and breakage of peptide bonds
Description: As outlined in additional specification guidance.

Name: Biological Molecules - Protein Structure Levels
Learning Outcomes: The levels of protein structure
Description: To include primary; secondary; tertiary and quaternary structure AND hydrogen bonding; hydrophobic and hydrophilic interactions; disulfide bonds and ionic bonds.

Name: Biological Molecules - Globular Proteins
Learning Outcomes: The structure and function of globular proteins including a conjugated protein
Description: To include haemoglobin as an example of a conjugated protein (globular protein with a prosthetic group); a named enzyme and insulin.

Name: Biological Molecules - Fibrous Proteins
Learning Outcomes: The properties and functions of fibrous proteins
Description: To include collagen; keratin and elastin (no details of structure are required).

Name: Biological Molecules - Inorganic Ions
Learning Outcomes: The key inorganic ions that are involved in biological processes
Description: To include the following: calcium ions (Ca2+), sodium ions (Na+), potassium ions (K+), hydrogen ions (H+), ammonium ions (NH4+), nitrate (NO3–), hydrogencarbonate (HCO3–), chloride (Cl –), phosphate (PO43–), hydroxide (OH–). Learners should be able to recognise the symbols for these ions.

Name: Biological Molecules - Biochemical Tests
Learning Outcomes: How to carry out and interpret the results of the chemical tests
Description: To include: biuret test for proteins; Benedict’s test for reducing and non-reducing sugars; iodine test for starch; emulsion test for lipids.

Name: Biological Molecules - Quantitative Concentration
Learning Outcomes: Quantitative methods to determine the concentration of a chemical substance in a solution
Description: To include colorimetry.

Name: Biological Molecules - Chromatography Principles
Learning Outcomes: The principles and uses of paper and thin layer chromatography to separate biological molecules / compounds
Description: To include calculation of Rf values (Rf = distance moved by the solute / distance moved by the solvent). Learners should be able to apply their knowledge and understanding in the context of separating proteins; carbohydrates; vitamins and nucleic acids.

Name: Biological Molecules - Chromatography Practical
Learning Outcomes: Practical investigations to analyse biological solutions using paper or thin layer chromatography
Description: As outlined in additional specification guidance.

Name: Nucleic Acids - Nucleotide Structure
Learning Outcomes: The structure of a nucleotide as the monomer from which nucleic acids are made
Description: To include the differences between RNA and DNA nucleotides; the identification of the purines and pyrimidines and the type of pentose sugar.

Name: Nucleic Acids - Phosphodiester Bonds
Learning Outcomes: The synthesis and breakdown of polynucleotides by the formation and breakage of phosphodiester bonds
Description: As outlined in additional specification guidance.

Name: Nucleic Acids - ADP and ATP
Learning Outcomes: The structure of ADP and ATP as phosphorylated nucleotides
Description: Comprising a pentose sugar (ribose); a nitrogenous base (adenine) and inorganic phosphates.

Name: Nucleic Acids - DNA Double Helix
Learning Outcomes: The structure of DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid)
Description: To include how hydrogen bonding between complementary base pairs (A to T; G to C) on two antiparallel DNA polynucleotides leads to the formation of a DNA molecule; and how the twisting of DNA produces its double-helix shape.

Name: Nucleic Acids - DNA Purification
Learning Outcomes: Practical investigations into the purification of DNA by precipitation
Description: As outlined in additional specification guidance.

Name: Nucleic Acids - Semi-Conservative Replication
Learning Outcomes: Semi-conservative DNA replication
Description: To include the roles of the enzymes helicase and DNA polymerase; the importance of replication in conserving genetic information with accuracy and the occurrence of random; spontaneous mutations.

Name: Nucleic Acids - Genetic Code Nature
Learning Outcomes: The nature of the genetic code
Description: To include the triplet; non-overlapping; degenerate and universal nature of the code and how a gene determines the sequence of amino acids in a polypeptide (the primary structure of a protein).

Name: Nucleic Acids - Protein Synthesis
Learning Outcomes: Transcription and translation of genes resulting in the synthesis of polypeptides
Description: To include; the roles of RNA polymerase, messenger (m)RNA, transfer (t)RNA, ribosomal (r)RNA.

Name: Enzymes - Metabolic Role
Learning Outcomes: The role of enzymes in catalysing reactions that affect metabolism at a cellular and whole organism level
Description: To include the idea that enzymes affect both structure and function.

Name: Enzymes - Intracellular and Extracellular
Learning Outcomes: The role of enzymes in catalysing both intracellular and extracellular reactions
Description: To include catalase as an example of an enzyme that catalyses intracellular reactions and amylase as an example of an enzyme that catalyses extracellular reactions.

Name: Enzymes - Action Mechanism
Learning Outcomes: The mechanism of enzyme action
Description: To include the tertiary structure; specificity; active site; lock and key hypothesis; induced-fit hypothesis; enzyme-substrate complex; enzyme-product complex; product formation and lowering of activation energy.

Name: Enzymes - Factors Affecting Activity
Learning Outcomes: The effects of pH temperature enzyme concentration and substrate concentration on enzyme activity
Description: To include reference to the temperature coefficient (Q10).

Name: Enzymes - Activity Investigations
Learning Outcomes: Practical investigations into the effects of pH temperature enzyme concentration and substrate concentration on enzyme activity
Description: Provides an opportunity for serial dilutions.

Name: Enzymes - Coenzymes and Cofactors
Learning Outcomes: The need for coenzymes and cofactors in some enzyme-controlled reactions
Description: To include the chloride ion as a cofactor for amylase and vitamins as a source of coenzymes.

Name: Enzymes - Inhibitors
Learning Outcomes: The effects of inhibitors on the rate of enzyme-controlled reactions
Description: To include competitive and non-competitive; reversible and non-reversible inhibitors; and the role of end-product inhibition.

Name: Membranes - Roles of Membranes
Learning Outcomes: The roles of membranes within cells and at the surface of cells
Description: To include the roles of membranes as: partially permeable barriers between the cell and its environment, between organelles and the cytoplasm and within organelles; sites of chemical reactions; sites of cell communication (cell signalling).

Name: Membranes - Fluid Mosaic Model
Learning Outcomes: The fluid mosaic model of membrane structure and the roles of its components
Description: To include phospholipids; cholesterol; glycolipids; proteins and glycoproteins AND the role of membrane-bound receptors as sites where hormones and drugs can bind.

Name: Membranes - Permeability Factors
Learning Outcomes: Factors affecting membrane structure and permeability
Description: To include the effects of temperature and solvents.

Name: Membranes - Permeability Investigations
Learning Outcomes: Practical investigations into factors affecting membrane structure and permeability
Description: As outlined in additional specification guidance.

Name: Membranes - Transport Methods
Learning Outcomes: The movement of molecules across membranes
Description: To include diffusion and facilitated diffusion as passive methods AND active transport; endocytosis and exocytosis as processes requiring adenosine triphosphate (ATP) as an immediate source of energy.

Name: Membranes - Diffusion Investigations
Learning Outcomes: Practical investigations into the factors affecting diffusion rates in model cells
Description: As outlined in additional specification guidance.

Name: Membranes - Osmosis Principles
Learning Outcomes: The movement of water across membranes by osmosis and the effects that solutions of different water potential can have on plant and animal cells
Description: Osmosis to be explained in terms of a water potential gradient across a partially-permeable membrane.

Name: Membranes - Osmosis Investigations
Learning Outcomes: Practical investigations into the effects of solutions of different water potential on plant and animal cells
Description: As outlined in additional specification guidance.

Name: Cell Division - Cell Cycle
Learning Outcomes: The cell cycle
Description: To include the processes taking place during interphase (G1; S and G2); mitosis and cytokinesis; leading to genetically identical cells.

Name: Cell Division - Regulation
Learning Outcomes: How the cell cycle is regulated
Description: To include an outline of the use of checkpoints to control the cycle.

Name: Cell Division - Mitosis Stages
Learning Outcomes: The main stages of mitosis
Description: To include the changes in the nuclear envelope; chromosomes; chromatids; centromere; centrioles; spindle fibres and cell membrane.

Name: Cell Division - Microscope Examination
Learning Outcomes: Sections of plant tissue showing the cell cycle and stages of mitosis
Description: To include the examination of stained sections and squashes of plant tissue and the production of labelled diagrams to show the stages observed.

Name: Cell Division - Mitosis Significance
Learning Outcomes: The significance of mitosis in life cycles
Description: To include growth; tissue repair and asexual reproduction in plants; animals and fungi.

Name: Cell Division - Meiosis Significance
Learning Outcomes: The significance of meiosis in life cycles
Description: To include the production of haploid cells and genetic variation by independent assortment and crossing over.

Name: Cell Division - Meiosis Stages
Learning Outcomes: The main stages of meiosis
Description: To include interphase; prophase 1; metaphase 1; anaphase 1; telophase 1; prophase 2; metaphase 2; anaphase 2; telophase 2 (no details of the names of the stages within prophase 1 are required) and the term homologous chromosomes.

Name: Cell Division - Specialised Cells
Learning Outcomes: How cells of multicellular organisms are specialised for particular functions
Description: To include erythrocytes; neutrophils; squamous and ciliated epithelial cells; sperm cells; palisade cells; root hair cells and guard cells.

Name: Cell Division - Cellular Organisation
Learning Outcomes: The organisation of cells into tissues organs and organ systems
Description: To include squamous and ciliated epithelia; cartilage; muscle; xylem and phloem as examples of tissues.

Name: Cell Division - Stem Cell Features
Learning Outcomes: The features and differentiation of stem cells
Description: To include stem cells as a renewing source of undifferentiated cells.

Name: Cell Division - Animal Differentiation
Learning Outcomes: The production of erythrocytes and neutrophils as examples of distinct differentiated cells derived from a common stem cell in bone marrow
Description: As outlined in additional specification guidance.

Name: Cell Division - Plant Differentiation
Learning Outcomes: The production of xylem vessels and phloem sieve tubes as examples of distinct differentiated outcomes derived from a common stem cell in meristems
Description: As outlined in additional specification guidance.

Name: Cell Division - Stem Cell Medical Uses
Learning Outcomes: The potential uses of stem cells in research and medicine
Description: To include the repair of damaged tissues; the treatment of neurological conditions and research into developmental biology. Learners are not required to recall specific neurological conditions.

Name: Exchange Surfaces - Specialised Surfaces
Learning Outcomes: The need for specialised exchange surfaces
Description: To include surface area to volume ratio (SA:V); metabolic activity; single-celled and multicellular organisms. (ratio = surface area / volume)

Name: Exchange Surfaces - Efficient Surface Features
Learning Outcomes: The features of an efficient exchange surface
Description: To include: increased surface area – root hair cells; thin layer – alveoli; good blood supply/ventilation to maintain gradient – gills/alveolus.

Name: Exchange Surfaces - Mammalian System Components
Learning Outcomes: The structures and functions of the components of the mammalian gaseous exchange system
Description: To include the distribution and functions of cartilage; ciliated epithelium; goblet cells; smooth muscle and elastic fibres in the trachea; bronchi; bronchioles and alveoli.

Name: Exchange Surfaces - Mammalian Ventilation
Learning Outcomes: The mechanism of ventilation in mammals
Description: To include the function of the rib cage; intercostal muscles (internal and external) and diaphragm.

Name: Exchange Surfaces - Spirometry Data
Learning Outcomes: The relationship between vital capacity; tidal volume; breathing rate and oxygen uptake
Description: To include analysis and interpretation of primary and secondary data e.g. from a data logger or spirometer.

Name: Exchange Surfaces - Fish and Insect Ventilation
Learning Outcomes: The mechanisms of ventilation and gas exchange in bony fish and insects
Description: To include: bony fish – changes in volume of the buccal cavity and the functions of the operculum; gill filaments and gill lamellae (gill plates); countercurrent flow; insects – spiracles; trachea; thoracic and abdominal movement to change body volume; exchange with tracheal fluid.

Name: Exchange Surfaces - Dissection and Drawing
Learning Outcomes: The dissection examination and drawing of the gaseous exchange system of a bony fish and/or insect trachea
Description: As outlined in additional specification guidance.

Name: Exchange Surfaces - Histology Slides
Learning Outcomes: The examination of microscope slides to show the histology of exchange surfaces
Description: As outlined in additional specification guidance.

Name: Transport in Animals - Need for Transport Systems
Learning Outcomes: The need for transport systems in multicellular animals
Description: To include an appreciation of size; metabolic rate and surface area to volume ratio (SA:V).

Name: Transport in Animals - Circulatory System Types
Learning Outcomes: The different types of circulatory systems
Description: To include single; double; open and closed circulatory systems in insects; fish and mammals.

Name: Transport in Animals - Blood Vessels
Learning Outcomes: The structure and functions of arteries; arterioles; capillaries; venules and veins
Description: To include the distribution of different tissues within the vessel walls.

Name: Transport in Animals - Tissue Fluid Formation
Learning Outcomes: The formation of tissue fluid from plasma
Description: To include reference to hydrostatic pressure; oncotic pressure and an explanation of the differences in the composition of blood; tissue fluid and lymph.

Name: Transport in Animals - Heart Anatomy
Learning Outcomes: The external and internal structure of the mammalian heart
Description: As outlined in additional specification guidance.

Name: Transport in Animals - Heart Dissection
Learning Outcomes: The dissection examination and drawing of the external and internal structure of the mammalian heart
Description: As outlined in additional specification guidance.

Name: Transport in Animals - Cardiac Cycle
Learning Outcomes: The cardiac cycle
Description: To include the role of the valves and the pressure changes occurring in the heart and associated vessels. (cardiac output = heart rate x stroke volume)

Name: Transport in Animals - Cardiac Coordination
Learning Outcomes: How heart action is initiated and coordinated
Description: To include the roles of the sino-atrial node (SAN); atrio-ventricular node (AVN); purkyne tissue and the myogenic nature of cardiac muscle (no detail of hormonal and nervous control is required at AS level).

Name: Transport in Animals - ECG Interpretation
Learning Outcomes: The use and interpretation of electrocardiogram (ECG) traces
Description: To include normal and abnormal heart activity (tachycardia; bradycardia; fibrillation and ectopic heartbeat only).

Name: Transport in Animals - Gas Transport Mechanisms
Learning Outcomes: The role of haemoglobin in transporting oxygen and carbon dioxide
Description: To include the reversible binding of oxygen molecules; carbonic anhydrase; haemoglobinic acid; hydrogencarbonate ion and the chloride shift.

Name: Transport in Animals - Dissociation Curves
Learning Outcomes: The oxygen dissociation curve for fetal and adult human haemoglobin
Description: To include the significance of the different affinities for oxygen AND the changes to the dissociation curve at different carbon dioxide concentrations (the Bohr effect).

Name: Transport in Plants - Need for Plant Transport
Learning Outcomes: The need for transport systems in multicellular plants
Description: To include an appreciation of size; metabolic rate and surface area to volume ratio (SA:V).

Name: Transport in Plants - Vascular System Anatomy
Learning Outcomes: The structure and function of the vascular system in the roots stems and leaves of herbaceous dicotyledonous plants
Description: To include xylem vessels; sieve tube elements and companion cells.

Name: Transport in Plants - Stained Tissue Distribution
Learning Outcomes: The examination and drawing of stained sections of plant tissue to show the distribution of xylem and phloem
Description: As outlined in additional specification guidance.

Name: Transport in Plants - Stem Dissection
Learning Outcomes: The dissection of stems both longitudinally and transversely and their examination to demonstrate the position and structure of xylem vessels
Description: As outlined in additional specification guidance.

Name: Transport in Plants - Transpiration Principles
Learning Outcomes: The process of transpiration and the environmental factors that affect transpiration rate
Description: To include an appreciation that transpiration is a consequence of gaseous exchange.

Name: Transport in Plants - Transpiration Practical
Learning Outcomes: Practical investigations to estimate transpiration rates
Description: To include the use of a potometer.

Name: Transport in Plants - Pathways and Mechanisms
Learning Outcomes: The transport of water into the plant through the plant and to the air surrounding the leaves
Description: To include details of the pathways taken by water (apoplast and symplast pathways only) AND the mechanisms of movement in terms of water potential; adhesion; cohesion and the transpiration stream.

Name: Transport in Plants - Environmental Adaptations
Learning Outcomes: Adaptations of plants to the availability of water in their environment
Description: To include xerophytes (cacti and marram grass) and hydrophytes (water lilies).

Name: Transport in Plants - Translocation Mechanism
Learning Outcomes: The mechanism of translocation
Description: To include translocation as an energy-requiring process transporting assimilates; especially sucrose; in the phloem between sources (e.g. leaves) and sinks (e.g. roots; meristem) AND details of active loading at the source and removal at the sink.

Name: Communicable Diseases - Pathogen Types
Learning Outcomes: The different types of pathogen that can cause communicable diseases in plants and animals
Description: To include: bacteria – tuberculosis (TB), ring rot (potatoes); viruses – HIV/AIDS (human), influenza (animals), Tobacco Mosaic Virus (plants); protoctista – malaria, potato/tomato late blight; fungi – black sigatoka (bananas), athlete’s foot (humans).

Name: Communicable Diseases - Transmission
Learning Outcomes: The means of transmission of animal and plant communicable pathogens
Description: To include an understanding of the different methods of transmission with reference to vectors
column5: spores and living conditions – e.g. climate

Name: Communicable Diseases - Plant Defences
Learning Outcomes: Plant defences against pathogens
Description: To include production of chemicals AND plant responses that limit the spread of the pathogen (e.g. callose deposition).

Name: Communicable Diseases - Primary Non-Specific Defences
Learning Outcomes: The primary non-specific defences against pathogens in animals
Description: Non-specific defences to include skin
column5: blood clotting (platelets releasing substances that via a cascade result in fibrin formation
column6: trapping platelets and forming a clot)

Name: Communicable Diseases - Phagocyte Mode of Action
Learning Outcomes: The structure and mode of action of phagocytes
Description: To include neutrophils and antigen-presenting cells AND the roles of cytokines

Name: Communicable Diseases - Blood Smears Examination
Learning Outcomes: Examination and drawing of cells observed in blood smears
Description: As outlined in additional specification guidance.

Name: Communicable Diseases - Lymphocytes
Learning Outcomes: The structure different roles and modes of action of B and T lymphocytes in the specific immune response
Description: To include the significance of cell signalling (reference to interleukins)
column7: T helper cells and T killer cells.

Name: Communicable Diseases - Immune Responses
Learning Outcomes: The primary and secondary immune responses
Description: To include T memory cells and B memory cells.

Name: Communicable Diseases - Antibody Structure
Learning Outcomes: The structure and general functions of antibodies
Description: To include the general protein structure of an antibody molecule.

Name: Communicable Diseases - Antibody Action
Learning Outcomes: An outline of the action of opsonins agglutinins and anti-toxins
Description: As outlined in additional specification guidance.

Name: Communicable Diseases - Types of Immunity
Learning Outcomes: The differences between active and passive immunity and between natural and artificial immunity
Description: To include examples of each type of immunity.

Name: Communicable Diseases - Autoimmune Diseases
Learning Outcomes: Autoimmune diseases
Description: To include an appreciation of the term autoimmune disease and arthritis as a named example.

Name: Communicable Diseases - Vaccination
Learning Outcomes: The principles of vaccination and the role of vaccination programmes in the prevention of epidemics
Description: To include routine vaccinations AND reasons for changes to vaccines and vaccination programmes (including global issues).

Name: Communicable Diseases - Medicine Sources
Learning Outcomes: Possible sources of medicines
Description: To include examples of microorganisms and plants (and so the need to maintain biodiversity) AND the potential for personalised medicines.

Name: Communicable Diseases - Antibiotic Benefits and Risks
Learning Outcomes: The benefits and risks of using antibiotics to manage bacterial infection
Description: To include the wide use of antibiotics following the discovery of penicillin in the mid-20th century AND the increase in bacterial resistance to antibiotics and its implications.

Name: Biodiversity - Levels of Biodiversity
Learning Outcomes: How biodiversity may be considered at different levels
Description: To include: habitat biodiversity (sand dunes, woodland, meadows, streams); species biodiversity (species richness and species evenness); genetic biodiversity (different breeds within a species).

Name: Biodiversity - Sampling Methods
Learning Outcomes: How sampling is used in measuring the biodiversity of a habitat and the importance of sampling
Description: To include how sampling can be carried out: random sampling and non-random sampling (opportunistic
column5: stratified and systematic) AND the importance of sampling the range of organisms in a habitat.

Name: Biodiversity - Field Practical Investigations
Learning Outcomes: Practical investigations collecting random and non-random samples in the field
Description: Techniques to include: quadrats

Name: Biodiversity - Richness and Evenness
Learning Outcomes: How to measure species richness and species evenness in a habitat
Description: As outlined in additional specification guidance.

Name: Biodiversity - Simpson Index
Learning Outcomes: The use and interpretation of Simpson’s Index of Diversity (D) to calculate the biodiversity of a habitat
Description: Formula provided where needed in assessments. To include the interpretation of both high and low values of Simpson’s Index of Diversity (D).

Name: Biodiversity - Assessing Genetic Diversity
Learning Outcomes: How genetic biodiversity may be assessed including calculations
Description: To include calculations of genetic diversity within isolated populations (proportion of polymorphic gene loci = number of polymorphic gene loci / total number of loci). Suitable populations include zoos

Name: Biodiversity - Factors Affecting Biodiversity
Learning Outcomes: The factors affecting biodiversity
Description: To include human population growth

Name: Biodiversity - Reasons for Maintenance
Learning Outcomes: The ecological economic and aesthetic reasons for maintaining biodiversity
Description: Ecological: protecting keystone species and maintaining genetic resource. Economic: reducing soil depletion. Aesthetic: protecting landscapes.

Name: Biodiversity - Conservation Methods
Learning Outcomes: In situ and ex situ methods of maintaining biodiversity
Description: In situ conservation: marine conservation zones and wildlife reserves. Ex situ conservation: seed banks

Name: Biodiversity - Conservation Agreements
Learning Outcomes: International and local conservation agreements made to protect species and habitats
Description: Historic and/or current agreements including CITES
column5: the Rio Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) and the Countryside Stewardship Scheme (CSS).

Name: Classification and Evolution - Taxonomic Hierarchy
Learning Outcomes: The biological classification of species
Description: To include the taxonomic hierarchy of kingdom

Name: Classification and Evolution - Binomial System
Learning Outcomes: The binomial system of naming species and the advantage of such a system
Description: As outlined in additional specification guidance.

Name: Classification and Evolution - Five Kingdoms
Learning Outcomes: The features used to classify organisms into the five kingdoms: Prokaryotae Protoctista Fungi Plantae Animalia
Description: To include the use of similarities in observable features in original classification.

Name: Classification and Evolution - Three Domains
Learning Outcomes: The evidence that has led to new classification systems such as the three domains of life which clarifies relationships
Description: To include the more recent use of similarities in biological molecules and other genetic evidence AND details of the three domains and a comparison of the kingdom and domain classification systems.

Name: Classification and Evolution - Phylogeny
Learning Outcomes: The relationship between classification and phylogeny
Description: Learners are not required to know cladistics.

Name: Classification and Evolution - Evidence for Evolution
Learning Outcomes: The evidence for the theory of evolution by natural selection
Description: To include the contributions of Darwin and Wallace in formulating the theory of evolution by natural selection AND fossil
column5: DNA (only genomic DNA at AS level) and molecular evidence.

Name: Classification and Evolution - Variation Types
Learning Outcomes: The different types of variation
Description: To include intraspecific and interspecific variation AND the differences between continuous and discontinuous variation AND both genetic and environmental causes of variation.

Name: Classification and Evolution - Adaptations
Learning Outcomes: The different types of adaptations of organisms to their environment
Description: Anatomical
column5: physiological and behavioural adaptations AND why organisms from different taxonomic groups may show similar anatomical features.

Name: Classification and Evolution - Natural Selection Mechanism
Learning Outcomes: The mechanism by which natural selection can affect the characteristics of a population over time
Description: To include an appreciation that genetic variation
column5: selection pressure and reproductive success (or failure) results in an increased proportion of the population possessing the advantageous characteristic(s).

Name: Classification and Evolution - Implications for Humans
Learning Outcomes: How evolution in some species has implications for human populations
Description: To include the evolution of pesticide resistance in insects and drug resistance in microorganisms.

Name: Communication and Homeostasis - Need for Communication
Learning Outcomes: The need for communication systems in multicellular organisms
Description: To include the need for animals and plants to respond to changes in the internal and external environment and to coordinate the activities of different organs.

Name: Communication and Homeostasis - Cell Signalling
Learning Outcomes: The communication between cells by cell signalling
Description: To include signalling between adjacent cells and signalling between distant cells.

Name: Communication and Homeostasis - Principles of Homeostasis
Learning Outcomes: The principles of homeostasis
Description: To include the differences between receptors and effectors and the differences between negative feedback and positive feedback.

Name: Communication and Homeostasis - Thermoregulation
Learning Outcomes: The physiological and behavioural responses involved in temperature control in ectotherms and endotherms
Description: To include endotherms – peripheral temperature receptors the role of the hypothalamus and effectors in skin and muscles; behavioural responses; ectotherms – behavioural responses.

Name: Excretion - Importance of Excretion
Learning Outcomes: The term excretion and its importance in maintaining metabolism and homeostasis
Description: To include reference to the importance of removing metabolic wastes including carbon dioxide and nitrogenous waste from the body.

Name: Excretion - Liver Anatomy and Function
Learning Outcomes: The structure and functions of the mammalian liver
Description: To include the gross structure and histology of the liver AND the roles of the liver in: storage of glycogen; detoxification; the formation of urea from ammonia reacting with carbon dioxide as part of the ornithine cycle.

Name: Excretion - Liver Histology Practical
Learning Outcomes: The examination and drawing of stained sections to show the histology of liver tissue
Description: As outlined in additional specification guidance.

Name: Excretion - Kidney Anatomy and Mechanism
Learning Outcomes: The structure mechanisms of action and functions of the mammalian kidney
Description: To include the gross structure and histology of the kidney including the detailed structure of a nephron and its associated blood vessels AND the processes of ultrafiltration selective reabsorption and the production of urine.

Name: Excretion - Kidney Dissection
Learning Outcomes: The dissection examination and drawing of the external and internal structure of the kidney
Description: As outlined in additional specification guidance.

Name: Excretion - Nephron Histology Practical
Learning Outcomes: The examination and drawing of stained sections to show the histology of nephrons
Description: As outlined in additional specification guidance.

Name: Excretion - Blood Water Potential Control
Learning Outcomes: The control of the water potential of the blood
Description: To include the role of osmoreceptors in the hypothalamus the posterior pituitary gland ADH and its effect on the walls of the collecting ducts.

Name: Excretion - Kidney Failure and Treatments
Learning Outcomes: The effects of kidney failure and its potential treatments
Description: To include the problems that arise from kidney failure including the effect on glomerular filtration rate (GFR) and electrolyte balance AND the use of renal dialysis (haemodialysis only) and transplants for the treatment of kidney failure.

Name: Excretion - Medical Diagnosis via Urine
Learning Outcomes: How excretory products can be used in medical diagnosis
Description: To include the use of urine samples in diagnostic tests with reference to the use of monoclonal antibodies in pregnancy testing and testing for anabolic steroids and drugs.

Name: Neuronal Communication - Sensory Receptors
Learning Outcomes: The roles of mammalian sensory receptors in converting different types of stimuli into nerve impulses
Description: To include an outline of the roles of sensory receptors (e.g. Pacinian corpuscle) in responding to specific types of stimuli and their roles as transducers.

Name: Neuronal Communication - Neurone Types
Learning Outcomes: The structure and functions of sensory relay and motor neurones
Description: To include differences between the structure and function of myelinated and non-myelinated neurones.

Name: Neuronal Communication - Nerve Impulse Generation
Learning Outcomes: The generation and transmission of nerve impulses in mammals
Description: To include how the resting potential is established and maintained and how an action potential is generated (including reference to positive feedback) and transmitted in a myelinated neurone AND the significance of the frequency of impulse transmission.

Name: Neuronal Communication - Synaptic Transmission
Learning Outcomes: The structure and roles of synapses in neurotransmission
Description: To include the structure of a cholinergic synapse; the action of neurotransmitters at the synapse; the importance of synapses in summation; inhibitory and excitatory synapses.

Name: Hormonal Communication - Endocrine Principles
Learning Outcomes: Endocrine communication by hormones
Description: To include secretion of hormones into the blood transport by the blood and detection by target cells or tissues.

Name: Hormonal Communication - Adrenal Glands
Learning Outcomes: The structure and functions of the adrenal glands
Description: Adrenal glands as an example of endocrine glands to include the hormones secreted by the cortex and medulla and their functions.

Name: Hormonal Communication - Pancreas Histology
Learning Outcomes: The histology of the pancreas
Description: To include the endocrine tissues.

Name: Hormonal Communication - Pancreas Examination
Learning Outcomes: The examination and drawing of stained sections of the pancreas to show the histology of the endocrine tissues
Description: As outlined in additional specification guidance.

Name: Hormonal Communication - Blood Glucose Regulation
Learning Outcomes: How blood glucose concentration is regulated
Description: To include the action of insulin and glucagon as an example of negative feedback and the role of the liver AND the control of insulin secretion with reference to potassium channels and calcium channels in the beta cells of the pancreas.

Name: Hormonal Communication - Diabetes Types
Learning Outcomes: The differences between Type 1 and Type 2 diabetes mellitus
Description: To include the causes of Type 1 and Type 2 diabetes and the treatments used for each.

Name: Hormonal Communication - Diabetes Treatments
Learning Outcomes: The potential treatments for diabetes mellitus
Description: To include the use of insulin produced by genetically modified bacteria and the potential use of stem cells to treat diabetes mellitus.

Name: Plant and Animal Responses - Plant Response Types
Learning Outcomes: The types of plant responses
Description: Plant response to abiotic stress and herbivory. Herbivory response to include chemical defences (alkaloids and pheromones only) and folding in response to touch AND the range of tropisms in plants.

Name: Plant and Animal Responses - Tropism Practical
Learning Outcomes: Practical investigations into phototropism and geotropism
Description: As outlined in additional specification guidance.

Name: Plant and Animal Responses - Plant Hormone Roles
Learning Outcomes: The roles of plant hormones
Description: To include the role of hormones in leaf loss in deciduous plants seed germination and stomatal closure.

Name: Plant and Animal Responses - Apical Dominance Evidence
Learning Outcomes: The experimental evidence for the role of auxins in the control of apical dominance
Description: To include the effects of auxin concentration on apical dominance. Learners should be able to apply their knowledge to different experiments.

Name: Plant and Animal Responses - Stem Elongation Evidence
Learning Outcomes: The experimental evidence for the role of gibberellin in the control of stem elongation and seed germination
Description: To include the effects of gibberellin concentration on stem elongation. Learners should be able to apply their knowledge to different experiments.

Name: Plant and Animal Responses - Growth Investigations
Learning Outcomes: Practical investigations into the effect of plant hormones on growth
Description: Provides an opportunity for serial dilution.

Name: Plant and Animal Responses - Commercial Use of Hormones
Learning Outcomes: The commercial use of plant hormones
Description: To include the use of hormones to control ripening the use of rooting powders and hormonal weed killers.

Name: Plant and Animal Responses - Mammalian Nervous System
Learning Outcomes: The organisation of the mammalian nervous system
Description: To include the structural organisation of the nervous system into the central and peripheral systems AND the functional organisation into the somatic and autonomic nervous systems.

Name: Plant and Animal Responses - Brain Structure
Learning Outcomes: The structure of the human brain and the functions of its parts
Description: To include the gross structure of the human brain AND the functions of the cerebrum cerebellum medulla oblongata hypothalamus and pituitary gland.

Name: Plant and Animal Responses - Reflex Actions
Learning Outcomes: Reflex actions
Description: To include knee jerk reflex with reference to the survival value of reflex actions.

Name: Plant and Animal Responses - System Coordination
Learning Outcomes: The coordination of responses by the nervous and endocrine systems
Description: To include the fight or flight response to environmental stimuli in mammals AND the action of hormones in cell signalling (studied in outline only) with reference to adrenaline (first messenger) activation of adenylyl cyclase and cyclic AMP (second messenger).

Name: Plant and Animal Responses - Heart Rate Control
Learning Outcomes: The effects of hormones and nervous mechanisms on heart rate
Description: An opportunity to monitor physiological functions for example with pulse rate measurements before during and after exercise or sensors to record electrical activity in the heart.

Name: Plant and Animal Responses - Muscle Structure and Contraction
Learning Outcomes: The structure of mammalian muscle and the mechanism of muscular contraction
Description: To include the structural and functional differences between skeletal involuntary and cardiac muscle AND the action of neuromuscular junctions AND the sliding filament model of muscular contraction and the role of ATP and how the supply of ATP is maintained in muscles by creatine phosphate.

Name: Plant and Animal Responses - Muscle Histology
Learning Outcomes: The examination of stained sections or photomicrographs of skeletal muscle
Description: As outlined in additional specification guidance.

Name: Photosynthesis - Respiration Interrelationship
Learning Outcomes: The interrelationship between the process of photosynthesis and respiration
Description: To include the relationship between the raw materials and products of the two processes.

Name: Photosynthesis - Chloroplast Structure
Learning Outcomes: The structure of a chloroplast and the sites of the two main stages of photosynthesis
Description: The components of a chloroplast including outer membrane lamellae grana thylakoid stroma and DNA.

Name: Photosynthesis - Photosynthetic Pigments
Learning Outcomes: The importance of photosynthetic pigments in photosynthesis
Description: To include reference to light harvesting systems and photosystems.

Name: Photosynthesis - Pigment Chromatography
Learning Outcomes: Practical investigations using thin layer chromatography (TLC) to separate photosynthetic pigments
Description: As outlined in additional specification guidance.

Name: Photosynthesis - Light-Dependent Stage
Learning Outcomes: The light-dependent stage of photosynthesis
Description: To include how energy from light is harvested and used to drive the production of chemicals which can be used as a source of energy for other metabolic processes (ATP and reduced NADP) with reference to electron carriers and cyclic and non-cyclic photophosphorylation AND the role of water.

Name: Photosynthesis - Light-Independent Stage
Learning Outcomes: The fixation of carbon dioxide and the light-independent stage of photosynthesis
Description: To include how the products of the light-dependent stage are used in the light-independent stage (Calvin cycle) to produce triose phosphate (TP) with reference to ribulose bisphosphate (RuBP) ribulose bisphosphate carboxylase (RuBisCO) and glycerate 3-phosphate (GP) – no other biochemical detail is required.

Name: Photosynthesis - Triose Phosphate Uses
Learning Outcomes: The uses of triose phosphate (TP)
Description: To include the use of TP as a starting material for the synthesis of carbohydrates lipids and amino acids AND the recycling of TP to regenerate the supply of RuBP.

Name: Photosynthesis - Limiting Factors
Learning Outcomes: Factors affecting photosynthesis
Description: To include limiting factors in photosynthesis with reference to carbon dioxide concentration light intensity and temperature and the implications of water stress (stomatal closure) AND the effect on the rate of photosynthesis and on levels of GP RuBP and TP of changing carbon dioxide concentration light intensity and temperature.

Name: Photosynthesis - Rate Investigations
Learning Outcomes: Practical investigations into factors affecting the rate of photosynthesis
Description: As outlined in additional specification guidance.

Name: Respiration - Need for Cellular Respiration
Learning Outcomes: The need for cellular respiration
Description: To include examples of why plants animals and microorganisms need to respire (suitable examples could include active transport and an outline of named metabolic reactions).

Name: Respiration - Mitochondrion Structure
Learning Outcomes: The structure of the mitochondrion
Description: The components of a mitochondrion including inner and outer mitochondrial membranes cristae matrix and mitochondrial DNA.

Name: Respiration - Glycolysis
Learning Outcomes: The process and site of glycolysis
Description: To include the phosphorylation of glucose to hexose bisphosphate the splitting of hexose bisphosphate into two triose phosphate molecules and further oxidation to pyruvate AND the production of a small yield of ATP and reduced NAD.

Name: Respiration - Link Reaction
Learning Outcomes: The link reaction and its site in the cell
Description: To include the formation of Acetyl CoA by the decarboxylation of pyruvate and the reduction of NAD to reduced NAD.

Name: Respiration - Krebs Cycle
Learning Outcomes: The process and site of the Krebs cycle
Description: To include the formation of citrate from the acetyl group of acetyl CoA and oxaloacetate and the reconversion of citrate to oxaloacetate (names of intermediate compounds are not required) AND the importance of decarboxylation dehydrogenation the reduction of NAD and FAD and substrate level phosphorylation.

Name: Respiration - Coenzymes Role
Learning Outcomes: The importance of coenzymes in cellular respiration
Description: With reference to NAD FAD and coenzyme A.

Name: Respiration - Oxidative Phosphorylation
Learning Outcomes: The process and site of oxidative phosphorylation
Description: To include the roles of electron carriers oxygen and the mitochondrial cristae.

Name: Respiration - Chemiosmotic Theory
Learning Outcomes: The chemiosmotic theory
Description: To include the electron transport chain proton gradients and ATP synthase in oxidative phosphorylation and photophosphorylation.

Name: Respiration - Anaerobic Respiration
Learning Outcomes: The process of anaerobic respiration in eukaryotes
Description: To include anaerobic respiration in mammals and yeast and the benefits of being able to respire anaerobically AND why anaerobic respiration produces a much lower yield of ATP than aerobic respiration.

Name: Respiration - Yeast Respiration Practical
Learning Outcomes: Practical investigations into respiration rates in yeast under aerobic and anaerobic conditions
Description: As outlined in additional specification guidance.

Name: Respiration - Respiratory Substrates
Learning Outcomes: The difference in relative energy values of carbohydrates lipids and proteins as respiratory substrates
Description: As outlined in additional specification guidance.

Name: Respiration - Respiratory Quotient
Learning Outcomes: The use and interpretation of the respiratory quotient (RQ)
Description: To include calculating the respiratory quotient (RQ) using the formula: RQ = CO2 produced / O2 consumed.

Name: Respiration - Rate Variation Practical
Learning Outcomes: Practical investigations into the effect of factors such as temperature substrate concentration and different respiratory substrates on the rate of respiration
Description: To include the use of respirometers.

Name: Cellular Control - Mutation Types
Learning Outcomes: Types of gene mutations and their possible effects on protein production and function
Description: To include substitution; insertion or deletion of one or more nucleotides AND the possible effects of these gene mutations (i.e. beneficial; neutral or harmful).

Name: Cellular Control - Gene Expression Regulation
Learning Outcomes: The regulatory mechanisms that control gene expression at the transcriptional level; post-transcriptional level and post-translational level
Description: To include control at the: transcriptional level (lac operon and general role of transcription factors); post-transcriptional level (editing of primary mRNA and removal of introns); post-translational level (activation of proteins by cyclic AMP).

Name: Cellular Control - Body Plan Development
Learning Outcomes: The genetic control of the development of body plans in different organisms
Description: The Homeobox gene sequences are similar and highly conserved in plants; animals and fungi and are involved in regulating gene expression AND the role of Hox genes (as a subset of Homeobox genes) in controlling body plan development.

Name: Cellular Control - Mitosis and Apoptosis
Learning Outcomes: The importance of mitosis and apoptosis as mechanisms controlling the development of body form
Description: To include an appreciation that the genes which regulate the cell cycle and apoptosis are able to respond to internal and external cell stimuli.

Name: Patterns of Inheritance - Phenotypic Variation
Learning Outcomes: The contribution of both environmental and genetic factors to phenotypic variation
Description: To include examples of both genetic and environmental contributions (e.g. diet in animals and etiolation in plants).

Name: Patterns of Inheritance - Genetic Variation Origin
Learning Outcomes: How sexual reproduction can lead to genetic variation within a species
Description: Meiosis and the random fusion of gametes at fertilisation.

Name: Patterns of Inheritance - Genetic Diagrams
Learning Outcomes: Genetic diagrams to show patterns of inheritance
Description: To include monogenic inheritance; dihybrid inheritance; multiple alleles; sex linkage and codominance.

Name: Patterns of Inheritance - Ratios and Epistasis
Learning Outcomes: The use of phenotypic ratios to identify linkage (autosomal and sex linkage) and epistasis
Description: To include explanations of linkage and epistasis.

Name: Patterns of Inheritance - Chi-Squared Test
Learning Outcomes: Using the chi-squared (x2) test to determine the significance of the difference between observed and expected results
Description: The formula for the chi-squared test will be provided: x2 = sum of ((o - e)^2 / e).

Name: Patterns of Inheritance - Continuous vs Discontinuous
Learning Outcomes: The genetic basis of continuous and discontinuous variation
Description: To include reference to the number of genes that influence each type of variation.

Name: Patterns of Inheritance - Evolutionary Factors
Learning Outcomes: The factors that can affect the evolution of a species
Description: To include stabilising selection and directional selection; genetic drift; genetic bottleneck and founder effect.

Name: Patterns of Inheritance - Hardy-Weinberg Principle
Learning Outcomes: The use of the Hardy-Weinberg principle to calculate allele frequencies in populations
Description: Equations provided where needed in assessments (p^2 + 2pq + q^2 = 1 and p + q = 1).

Name: Patterns of Inheritance - Speciation Isolating Mechanisms
Learning Outcomes: The role of isolating mechanisms in the evolution of new species
Description: To include geographical mechanisms (allopatric speciation) and reproductive mechanisms (sympatric speciation).

Name: Patterns of Inheritance - Artificial Selection Principles
Learning Outcomes: The principles of artificial selection and its uses
Description: To include examples of selective breeding in plants and animals AND an appreciation of the importance of maintaining a resource of genetic material for use in selective breeding including wild types.

Name: Patterns of Inheritance - Artificial Selection Ethics
Learning Outcomes: The ethical considerations surrounding the use of artificial selection
Description: To include a consideration of the more extreme examples of the use of artificial selection to 'improve' domestic species e.g. dog breeds.

Name: Manipulating Genomes - DNA Sequencing Principles
Learning Outcomes: The principles of DNA sequencing and new DNA sequencing techniques
Description: To include the rapid advancements of the techniques used in sequencing from Sanger sequencing to high throughput sequencing. Learners are not required to know details of high throughput sequencing techniques.

Name: Manipulating Genomes - Genome Comparisons
Learning Outcomes: How gene sequencing has allowed for genome-wide comparisons between individuals and between species
Description: With reference to bioinformatics and computational biology and how these fields are contributing to biological research into genotype-phenotype relationships; epidemiology and searching for evolutionary relationships.

Name: Manipulating Genomes - Amino Acid Prediction
Learning Outcomes: How gene sequencing has allowed for the sequences of amino acids in polypeptides to be predicted
Description: As outlined in additional specification guidance.

Name: Manipulating Genomes - Synthetic Biology
Learning Outcomes: How gene sequencing has allowed for the development of synthetic biology
Description: As outlined in additional specification guidance.

Name: Manipulating Genomes - DNA Profiling
Learning Outcomes: The principles of DNA profiling and its uses
Description: To include forensics and analysis of disease risk.

Name: Manipulating Genomes - PCR Principles
Learning Outcomes: The principles of the polymerase chain reaction (PCR) and its application in DNA analysis
Description: As outlined in additional specification guidance.

Name: Manipulating Genomes - Electrophoresis
Learning Outcomes: The principles and uses of electrophoresis for separating nucleic acid fragments or proteins
Description: Opportunity for practical use of electrophoresis.

Name: Manipulating Genomes - Genetic Engineering Principles
Learning Outcomes: The principles of genetic engineering
Description: To include the isolation of genes from one organism and the placing of these genes into another organism using suitable vectors.

Name: Manipulating Genomes - Genetic Engineering Techniques
Learning Outcomes: The techniques used in genetic engineering
Description: To include the use of restriction enzymes; plasmids and DNA ligase to form recombinant DNA with the desired gene and electroporation.

Name: Manipulating Genomes - Genetic Manipulation Ethics
Learning Outcomes: The ethical issues (both positive and negative) relating to the genetic manipulation of animals (including humans); plants and microorganisms
Description: To include insect resistance in genetically modified soya; genetically modified pathogens for research and 'pharming' (genetically modified animals to produce pharmaceuticals) AND issues relating to patenting and technology transfer.

Name: Manipulating Genomes - Gene Therapy
Learning Outcomes: The principles of and potential for gene therapy in medicine
Description: To include the differences between somatic cell gene therapy and germ line cell gene therapy.

Name: Cloning and Biotechnology - Natural Plant Clones
Learning Outcomes: Natural clones in plants and the production of natural clones for use in horticulture
Description: To include examples of natural cloning and the methods used to produce clones (various forms of vegetative propagation).

Name: Cloning and Biotechnology - Plant Cuttings
Learning Outcomes: How to take plant choosing as an example of a simple cloning technique
Description: Dissection of a selection of plant material to produce cuttings.

Name: Cloning and Biotechnology - Plant Micropropagation
Learning Outcomes: The production of artificial clones of plants by micropropagation and tissue culture
Description: As outlined in additional specification guidance.

Name: Cloning and Biotechnology - Plant Cloning Arguments
Learning Outcomes: The arguments for and against artificial cloning in plants
Description: To include an evaluation of the uses of plant cloning in horticulture and agriculture.

Name: Cloning and Biotechnology - Natural Animal Clones
Learning Outcomes: Natural clones in animal species
Description: To include examples of natural clones (twins formed by embryo splitting).

Name: Cloning and Biotechnology - Artificial Animal Cloning
Learning Outcomes: How artificial clones in animals can be produced by artificial embryo twinning or by enucleation and somatic cell nuclear transfer (SCNT)
Description: As outlined in additional specification guidance.

Name: Cloning and Biotechnology - Animal Cloning Arguments
Learning Outcomes: The arguments for and against artificial cloning in animals
Description: To include an evaluation of the uses of animal cloning (examples including in agriculture and medicine; and issues of longevity of cloned animals).

Name: Cloning and Biotechnology - Industrial Microorganisms
Learning Outcomes: The use of microorganisms in biotechnological processes
Description: To include reasons why microorganisms are used: economic considerations; short life cycle and growth requirements.

Name: Cloning and Biotechnology - Microorganisms as Food
Learning Outcomes: The advantages and disadvantages of using microorganisms to make food for human consumption
Description: To include bacterial and fungal sources.

Name: Cloning and Biotechnology - Culturing Microorganisms
Learning Outcomes: How to culture microorganisms effectively using aseptic techniques
Description: An opportunity for serial dilutions and culturing on agar plates.

Name: Cloning and Biotechnology - Fermentation Conditions
Learning Outcomes: The importance of manipulating the growing conditions in batch and continuous fermentation in order to maximise the yield of product required
Description: As outlined in additional specification guidance.

Name: Cloning and Biotechnology - Growth Curve Standard
Learning Outcomes: The standard growth curve of a microorganism in a closed culture
Description: To include the formula for number of individual organisms: N = N0 x 2^n.

Name: Cloning and Biotechnology - Growth Curve Investigations
Learning Outcomes: Practical investigations into the factors affecting the growth of microorganisms
Description: An opportunity for serial dilutions and the use of broth.

Name: Cloning and Biotechnology - Immobilised Enzymes
Learning Outcomes: The uses of immobilised enzymes in biotechnology and the different methods of immobilisation
Description: To include methods of enzyme immobilisation AND an evaluation of the use of immobilised enzymes in biotechnology (examples: glucose isomerase; penicillin acylase; lactase; aminoacylase; glucoamylase).

Name: Ecosystems - Dynamic Ecosystems
Learning Outcomes: Ecosystems which range in size are dynamic and are influenced by both biotic and abiotic factors
Description: To include reference to a variety of ecosystems of different sizes (e.g. a rock pool; a playing field; a large tree) and named examples of biotic and abiotic factors.

Name: Ecosystems - Biomass Transfers
Learning Outcomes: Biomass transfers through ecosystems
Description: To include how biomass transfers between trophic levels can be measured AND the efficiency of biomass transfers between trophic levels (efficiency = (biomass transferred / biomass intake) x 100) AND how human activities can manipulate the transfer of biomass through ecosystems.

Name: Ecosystems - Recycling Processes
Learning Outcomes: Recycling within ecosystems
Description: To include the role of decomposers and the roles of microorganisms in recycling nitrogen within ecosystems (including Nitrosomonas; Nitrobacter; Azotobacter and Rhizobium) AND the importance of the carbon cycle to include the role of organisms and physical/chemical effects.

Name: Ecosystems - Primary Succession
Learning Outcomes: The process of primary succession in the development of an ecosystem
Description: To include succession from pioneer species to a climax community AND deflected succession.

Name: Ecosystems - Measuring Ecosystems
Learning Outcomes: How the distribution and abundance of organisms in an ecosystem can be measured
Description: As outlined in additional specification guidance.

Name: Ecosystems - Sampling Methods
Learning Outcomes: The use of sampling and recording methods to determine the distribution and abundance of organisms in a variety of ecosystems
Description: As outlined in additional specification guidance.

Name: Populations and Sustainability - Population Size Factors
Learning Outcomes: The factors that determine size of a population
Description: To include the significance of limiting factors in determining the carrying capacity of a given environment and the impact of these factors on final population size.

Name: Populations and Sustainability - Population Interactions
Learning Outcomes: Interactions between populations
Description: To include predator–prey relationships considering the effects on both predator and prey populations AND interspecific and intraspecific competition.

Name: Populations and Sustainability - Conservation vs Preservation
Learning Outcomes: The reasons for and differences between conservation and preservation
Description: To include the economic; social and ethical reasons for conservation of biological resources.

Name: Populations and Sustainability - Sustainable Management
Learning Outcomes: How the management of an ecosystem can provide resources in a sustainable way
Description: Limited to management of ecosystems for timber production and fishing.

Name: Populations and Sustainability - Human Impacts
Learning Outcomes: The management of environmental resources and the effects of human activities
Description: To include how ecosystems can be managed to balance the conflict between conservation/preservation and human needs AND the effects of human activities on the animal and plant populations and how these are controlled.
